c.tagline: Tohoku castle town famous for a thousand cherry trees, apple orchards, and Meiji-era brick.

taxi.color: varies by company (often black or white)
taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered, clean, and reliable but pricier than buses for a regional city; the GO app helps hail one outside the station area.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 119 reaches ambulance/fire; English support is limited outside major cities, and the Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787) can help translate.

hood_desc: Hirosaki Park surrounds the city's iconic wooden castle keep and is Japan's cherry-blossom epicenter each spring, with moats, gardens, and museums; best for first-time visitors and sakura-season crowds.
A preserved row of Edo-period samurai houses and hedges just north of the castle, offering a quiet step into feudal-era Tsugaru domain life; suits history lovers and photographers.
The area around JR Hirosaki Station and the covered Dobashi shopping street, with everyday shops, apple-themed goods, and easy bus/train access; suits practical travelers who want to be near transit.

A cluster of Meiji- and Taisho-era Western-style buildings, including the former city library and a red-brick church, blending Japanese and European architecture; good for architecture fans and a relaxed stroll.
The rural foothills of Mount Iwaki, ringed by apple orchards and hot-spring inns, with views over the Tsugaru Plain; suits travelers wanting onsen relaxation and countryside scenery.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Japan.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 7am-9pm; JR trains run until about 10-11pm; there is no late-night service.
transit.pay: Suica/Pasmo-type IC cards work on JR trains; city buses are often cash or local-card only, so check before boarding.
transit.note: Hirosaki's castle and station areas are compact and very walkable; buses and short local rail lines connect outlying sights like Mount Iwaki and the apple orchards.

train: Shin-Aomori Shinkansen station (~40 min away) connects to Tokyo
bus: Highway buses to Aomori, Akita, Sendai, and Tokyo

transit.m: Airport limousine bus to Hirosaki Station (~55 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary and can cause confusion; good service is simply expected and included in the price.
